newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bank shares end up on "great week".
newsitem.headline: Beirut bank shares end up on "great week".

text.p: Bank shares soared on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Wednesday as Bank of Beirut consolidated an electrifying market debut.
"It's been a great week," Alain Balian, Deputy Manager at Lebanon Invest told Reuters, after all three listed bank shares rose strongly.
The LIBX bank index rose 6.37 percent to 131.10. The general BLOM stock index rose 0.55 percent to 913.57 and the LISPI moved up by 1.9 percent to 86.57.

Total turnover for the week, shortened to three days by the Moslem Eid al-Adha holiday, was 1,077,155 shares for a value of $8,708,534 against 1,097,912 shares and $8,283,253 during five days last week.
BOB, which made its debut last Friday, jumped to $3.375 from $3 on the week, for a 55.5 percent increase on its issue price.
Brokers said the new share's powerful performance boosted confidence in bank stocks in general and aroused massive interest in all listed shares that should continue next week.
"Confidence is growing in stocks in Lebanon. The process of investor shift to bank stocks as an investment alternative has begun in a very significant way," Balian said.
Of the two other bank shares, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose 4.3 percent to $15.125 from $14.5 Banque Audi rose 2.6 percent to $20 from $19.5.
BLC and Audi have risen 33 percent and 34 percent respectively since their debuts nearly four months ago.
Demand for BOB in the week ranged from 2.4 million to 5.4 million shares against supply of up to 135,000.
"I think the banks will continue rising next week. The market in general is on the rise," Balian said.
Turnover in Audi shares rose to 135,124 from 90,697 in the five trading days last week. Some 35,908 BLC shares were traded against last week's 28,404.
Solidere A and B were unchanged at $10.25 and $10.75 on turnover of 326,817 shares against 393,720 last week.
Markets will be closed on Thursday and Friday for the Moslem Eid al-Adha holiday.
Of the four industrial shares, Ciments Libanais rose to $1.28125 from $1.25, pipemaker Eternit was unchanged at $2 and Ciments Blancs was unchanged at $5.5.
There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic.
